claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: A shortest cycle remaining in G-S is induced and even. An induced even cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices, so the only possible lengths are 4, 6, and 8. Conversely, an FVS meets every such cycle. Each component after deleting an FVS is a tree; P8-freeness bounds its diameter by 6 and hence its radius by 3. For inclusion-minimal S, restoring any x creates a cycle through x whose other vertices form a path inside one component of G-S, giving two neighbors of x in that component.
claims.search_method: Direct shortest-cycle, tree-diameter, and minimality proof; checked the quantifiers for arbitrary S and every x in an inclusion-minimal S.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: Claim 0 converts FVS exactly into rank-at-most-eight hypergraph transversal. An unhit short induced cycle forces every solution to select one of at most eight vertices, yielding at most O(8^k) search nodes and O(n^8) detection work per node; iterative deepening gives an exact minimum solution when its size is at most k. For approximation, the union of a maximal vertex-disjoint packing of short induced cycles hits every such cycle. If the packing has p members, every FVS has size at least p and the returned union has size at most 8p.
claims.search_method: Direct branching-tree and packing lower-bound analysis.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: Independent exhaustive generation reproduced the ordered-graph counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. At each extension it forces the next Hamilton-path edge, enumerates every subset of allowable earlier opposite-parity neighbors, and rejects exactly graphs containing a C4 or induced P8. Thus no graph in the class has a 15-vertex simple path: the induced subgraph on such a path's vertices would occur in this exhaustive enumeration. An undirected DFS therefore has at most 14 vertices on a root-to-leaf path. Ancestor bags form a valid decomposition because every undirected DFS edge is ancestor-comparable, giving width at most 13. Standard fixed-width induced-forest/FVS dynamic programming is polynomial.
claims.witness: The exact count vector terminates with zero at order 15.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive enumeration followed by a direct DFS tree-decomposition proof.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: Branching on the four vertices of an uncovered C4, with iterative deepening, finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. Claim 2 gives a width-13 decomposition of G-X. Adding all r vertices of X to every bag gives width at most r+13. A standard FVS dynamic program records the deleted bag vertices and the connectivity partition of retained vertices, using 2^{O(r log r)} states per bag and rejecting transitions that close a cycle. Multiplying the bounds yields the stated FPT time.
claims.search_method: Checked the transversal branching, decomposition lifting, state sufficiency, and Bell-number state bound independently.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: In the half graph H_n, all open neighborhoods are distinct and the graph is P5-free. Retaining all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n shows a C4-transversal of size n-2; choosing the two least-index retained A vertices gives the matching lower bound. The graph of m internally disjoint length-three u-v paths is bipartite, 2-connected, C4-free, has order 2m+2, and is P8-free because an induced path can select at most two neighbors of either hub. Finally, on K_{3,3}, the integral short-cycle transversal optimum is 2 while the uniform assignment 1/4 has objective 3/2 and satisfies every C4 constraint.
claims.witness: The families are H_n, the length-three theta graphs, and K_{3,3} with x_v=1/4.
claims.search_method: Direct family analysis supplemented by exact checks of half graphs, theta graphs, and LP arithmetic.

claims.claim: Even false-twin-free P5-free bipartite graphs have simultaneously unbounded Feedback Vertex Set optimum and unbounded treewidth: for the half graph H_n, fvs(H_n)=n-2 and tw(H_n)≥⌈n/2⌉.
claims.evidence: The half graph's neighborhoods are strictly nested within each side, distinct across sides, and exclude an induced 2K2, hence it is false-twin-free and P5-free. Keeping all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n leaves a forest, proving fvs≤n-2. In any retained forest with at least two A vertices, let a_i,a_j be the two least-index retained vertices. C4-freeness permits at most one retained b_l with l≥j, so at most j B vertices and n-j+2 A vertices survive; at most n+2 vertices survive in total. The case with at most one A vertex deletes at least n-1 vertices. Hence fvs=n-2. With t=⌈n/2⌉, the indicated A and B subsets induce K_{t,n-t+1}, whose treewidth is t.
claims.witness: H_n; exact brute force confirmed fvs(H_n)=n-2 for 2≤n≤7.
claims.search_method: Direct nested-neighborhood and retained-forest counting proof, plus exact small-instance enumeration.

claims.claim: The natural induced-short-cycle covering LP has integrality gap tending to 2 already on P4-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n}, its integral optimum is n-1, its fractional optimum is n/2, and the ratio is 2-2/n.
claims.evidence: K_{n,n} is P4-free and its only induced cycles are C4s. Deleting at most n-2 vertices leaves at least two vertices on each side, hence a C4; deleting n-1 vertices from one side leaves a star. Thus the integral optimum is n-1. The uniform solution x_v=1/4 has value n/2. Summing all binom(n,2)^2 constraints, with every vertex occurring in (n-1)binom(n,2) constraints, proves every fractional solution has value at least n/2. The ratio is therefore (n-1)/(n/2)=2-2/n.
claims.witness: K_{n,n} with the uniform fractional assignment x_v=1/4.
claims.search_method: Exact double-counting proof and Fraction-arithmetic verification for 2≤n≤10.

claims.claim: The factor 8 for the specific maximal-short-cycle-packing union algorithm is tight on P8-free bipartite graphs.
claims.evidence: A disjoint union of t chordless C8 components is bipartite and induced-P8-free. Each component's only induced C4, C6, or C8 is its full C8, so every maximal packing contains all t components and its union has 8t vertices. One deletion per component is necessary and sufficient, making OPT=t and the algorithm's ratio exactly 8.
claims.witness: The disjoint union of t chordless C8 graphs.
claims.search_method: Direct induced-subgraph and packing analysis, with an exact C8 forest check.

claims.claim: False-twin quotienting exactly preserves the P8-free bipartite setting: contracting every equal-open-neighborhood class to one representative produces a false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeleton H with class multiplicities q_v, and every false-twin blow-up of such an H is again P8-free and bipartite.
claims.evidence: Equal-open-neighborhood classes are independent, and adjacency between distinct classes is complete or empty. Selecting one representative per class therefore makes H an induced subgraph, preserving bipartiteness and P8-freeness. Equal quotient neighborhoods would lift to equal unions of original classes, so H is false-twin-free. Blow-up preserves bipartiteness. An induced P8 cannot contain two members of one blown-up class because those members would be false twins in the induced subgraph, while P8 has no equal-open-neighborhood pair. Hence any induced P8 in a blow-up projects injectively and inducedly to H, contradicting P8-freeness of H.
claims.search_method: Direct quotient and injective-projection proof, including isolated-class and cross-class cases.

claims.claim:
Maximum induced forests admit an exact singleton-core/pendant-bundle normal form on the false-twin quotient. If H is the quotient and q_v is the size of class v, then
α_forest(G)=max_{U⊆V(H), H[U] a forest} (|U|+α_q(H[D_U])),
where D_U={v∉U:q_v>1 and |N_H(v)∩U|≤1} and α_q denotes maximum q-weight independent-set value.
claims.evidence: If an induced forest retains at least two vertices of a false-twin class, that class can have at most one retained neighbor vertex; otherwise two twins and two neighbors induce a C4. Any partially retained class with between 2 and q_v-1 vertices can consequently be saturated by adding leaves or isolates, so a maximum forest uses 0, 1, or q_v vertices per class. Singleton classes induce a forest U. Fully retained nonsingleton classes form an independent set and each has at most one neighbor in U, hence form an independent subset of D_U. Conversely, every such U and independent L⊆D_U expands to a forest because each full bundle supplies only leaves or isolates. Maximizing the q-weight of L proves the formula.
claims.witness: Independent exhaustive comparison of the formula with direct maximum-induced-forest enumeration passed on 5,518 small bipartite blow-ups.
claims.search_method: Complete saturation-and-converse proof, supplemented by exhaustive small-instance counterexample search.

claims.claim: The target is polynomial-time equivalent, with multiplicities measured in unary by Q=Σ_v q_v, to optimizing the quotient formula over false-twin-free P8-free bipartite skeletons; for every fixed singleton core U, the optimal pendant-bundle completion is computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Computing false-twin classes, their representatives, and multiplicities is polynomial and gives Q=|V(G)|. Claim 9 converts any quotient optimum back into an induced forest and hence an FVS. Conversely, unary multiplicities permit explicit polynomial-size blow-up; Claim 8 keeps the graph P8-free and bipartite, and an exact FVS solution recovers the quotient optimum. For fixed U, H[D_U] is bipartite. Maximum q-weight independent set equals total weight minus minimum q-weight vertex cover, which is obtained by an s-t cut using vertex-weight arcs and edge arcs of capacity greater than Σq_v. The remaining maximization over U is not solved by this reduction.
claims.witness: The two reductions are quotienting and unary blow-up; the completion subproblem is the standard weighted bipartite vertex-cover min-cut network.
claims.search_method: Checked encoding size, value and solution preservation, class preservation, and the weighted min-cut reduction independently.

target_evidence: The exact source target asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on all P8-free bipartite graphs. The draft proves material structural, approximation, parameterized, subclass, obstruction, and quotient-normal-form results, but neither the 8^k algorithm nor the C4-transversal-parameter algorithm is polynomial for unbounded parameters, and the width-13 result covers only the C4-free subclass. The quotient reformulation explicitly leaves selection of the singleton core U unresolved. Thus the work is correct substantive partial progress, not a proof of the full target, and the draft's PARTIAL resolution claim is accurate.
